raw_response:
Let me think through this as the farmer, then give the plan.

---

Well, another year. I'm 62 now, been doing this since my father handed me the hoe. My back isn't what it was, but I know this land.

I've got 10.9 mu altogether. I keep about 4 mu in cotton — that's the western plot, the soil there is okay for it. The rest, about 6.9 mu, I do wheat first and then flip to maize after harvest. That's what most people around here do. My neighbor Old Zhang does the same thing, been watching his fields for years.

My son works at the plastics factory in Handan most of the year. He comes back for wheat harvest, helps a few days. My daughter-in-law watches the grandchildren. So for the heavy work — especially cotton picking — it's mostly me and my wife, and sometimes my second daughter helps on weekends. Getting old is expensive when you can't do things yourself.

---

**Cotton (4 mu):**

I plant around April 20th, after Grain Rain. Too early and the cold can hurt the seedlings. I buy seed from the village shop — same kind I've been buying for five or six years. The boss there knows what works around here.

Before planting I plow the field and put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, mixed into the soil. When the bolls start forming in July, I'll topdress a little more — maybe half a bag of urea per mu if I have the cash. Cotton sucks a lot out of the soil.

For water, I pump twice — once in July when it gets really dry, once in August. Well water costs money every time the motor runs. I don't irrigate more than I have to.

Pests are the headache with cotton. Aphids every year, I spray when I see them clustering on the leaves. Sometimes bollworm too, I ask at the agro-supply shop what's working this year. I usually spray four or five times total.

Picking starts September, goes until October. It's the hardest part. Me, my wife, maybe my daughter. We pick over three or four times because the bolls don't all open at once. I'm hoping for 220 kg per mu, same as last year.

---

**Wheat (6.9 mu):**

I plant in early October, right around National Day holiday. I've been using the same variety for three years — the one Liu Guohua from the next village recommended. Good ears, doesn't fall over in wind.

I call the machine operator from the township to drill the seed in for me. I'm not planting by hand 7 mu at 62. He mixes in the compound fertilizer at the same time — I put down about one bag per mu (compound, the 15-15-15 kind). Then in late February, when the wheat is jointing and I can see if it looks yellow or not, I'll spread urea on top if it needs it. Some years I use half a bag per mu, some years a bit less.

I irrigate three times — first time in late November after it greens up, second time at jointing in March, third time when it flowers in April. That's pretty much what everyone does.

Herbicide once in winter when the weeds come up. Fungicide sometimes in April if the weather is wet and I'm worried about scab, but I ask around first.

Harvest is around June 5-10, the combine comes through the village. I try to get the wheat off in one day so I can plant maize right after.

I expect 380 kg per mu if the spring isn't too dry.

---

**Maize (6.9 mu, same fields right after wheat):**

This part makes me nervous every year. You've got maybe 4 or 5 days between wheat harvest and when you need to get maize in the ground. If you wait too long, the season is too short and the yield drops.

I buy hybrid seed — everyone uses it now, the extension station has been saying it for years. I plant by hand or hire someone with a small planter, depending on who's available. I put down compound fertilizer when planting, about half a bag per mu. Then when the plants are knee-high, I topdress with urea.

Summer rains usually help in July and August. I irrigate once for sure, maybe twice if August is dry. Less pumping cost than wheat or cotton.

I spray herbicide right after planting before it emerges. Maize borer sometimes shows up — I check and spray if I see the tunneling damage on the young stalks.

Harvest in late September, the combine comes again.

I expect 430 kg per mu. Last year was 440, so that's about right.

---

**My main worry this year:**

Fertilizer prices have gone up again. I'm going to be careful not to spend more than I have. My grandson is starting middle school in September — that costs money too. I'd rather apply a little less fertilizer and keep some cash in the house than borrow money to buy inputs. If wheat prices are good this summer I'll feel better about the maize fertilizer budget.
